notes: VERIFIER FIX (2026-09-17): status corrected 'approved' -> 'shutdown' (via a sourced 'active' interval 2022-2026, then Long Shutdown 3). The prior record's own note already stated 'approved' likely understated SND@LHC's true operating status; this fix resolves that by sourcing the operating interval to the collaboration's own 2023 PRL (arXiv:2305.09383), which states data were collected 'in 2022', and capping it at the LHC-wide Long Shutdown 3 boundary already used for ALICE/LHCb/TOTEM/FASER/LHCf in this partition.

VERIFIER-ADDED (2026-09-17): technology and the TI18/480 m placement are now independently corroborated by the SND@LHC detector-description paper (arXiv:2210.02784), which states the detector sits '480 m downstream of the ATLAS interaction point, in the TI18 tunnel' -- confirming the placement fact that the prior record could only support with 'general knowledge of the FASER/SND@LHC forward programme' (site:cern-ti18-snd-lhc notes still flag the coordinate itself, only its lat/lon, as unverified).

summary.plain: The SND@LHC detector sits in a disused CERN tunnel opposite FASER, built to catch neutrinos and rare particles from LHC collisions. It operated from 2022 until the LHC's current maintenance shutdown began in 2026.
summary.technical: Compact stand-alone detector in the TI18 tunnel, 480 m downstream of the ATLAS interaction point: an 830 kg tungsten target interleaved with emulsion and electronic trackers (also acting as an electromagnetic calorimeter), followed by a hadronic calorimeter and a muon identification system. Operated 2022 - June 2026; off since CERN's Long Shutdown 3 began.

technology.quote: The detector is composed of a hybrid system based on an 830 kg target made of tungsten plates, interleaved with emulsion and electronic trackers, also acting as an electromagnetic calorimeter, and followed by a hadronic calorimeter and a muon identification system.
